items.title: The first cohomology of the multiplicative group is the Picard group for all the big topologies
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter etale-cohomology.tex, section on comparing topologies
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem asserts a chain of canonical identifications H^1_{fppf}(X, G_m) = H^1_{syntomic}(X, G_m) = H^1_{smooth}(X, G_m) = H^1_etale(X, G_m) = H^1_{Zar}(X, G_m) = Pic(X) = H^1(X, O_X^*) for every scheme X (statement lines 2499-2507). The proof does not repeat the argument for each topology; it lets tau run over all the topologies considered in the big-and-small section and shows in one stroke that H^1_tau(X, G_m) = H^1_tau(X, O_tau^*) = Pic(O_tau) = Pic(X), where the middle step replaces the sheaf of units by the structure sheaf and the last step uses that invertible modules are quasi-coherent and that quasi-coherent modules are insensitive to the choice of topology (proof lines 2511-2525). What makes this short proof work is the recourse to the more precise descent proposition for quasi-coherent modules. The claim is H2: one uniform argument, three citations.
